files.summary: Switch names its button with aria-labelledby (visible label id), links the description with aria-describedby, and hides the knob with aria-hidden. Props unchanged.
Adds exported ACCESSIBILITY_STYLESHEET = './styles/accessibility.css' and a doc comment stating the shell import requirement. No other logic changed.

Forced-colors block: switch track gets a ButtonText border, knob gets a ButtonText fill (off and on), disabled knob gets GrayText. Rules are placed before the checked and disabled state rules so those still win.
20 static tests: rendered Switch markup via react-dom/server (bundled in memory), CSS forced-colors and reduced-motion declarations, focus outline, and src/main.tsx import order.

checks.note: Repo-local install in this worktree; node_modules is git-ignored.

interfaces.name: Switch
interfaces.props: { checked: boolean; onChange: (v: boolean) => void; label: string; description?: string; disabled?: boolean }
interfaces.markup: <label id="{id}-label" for="{id}"> names <button id="{id}" role="switch" aria-labelledby="{id}-label" aria-describedby="{id}-description"> (description only when given). The knob span is aria-hidden.
interfaces.note: Callers need no change. Disabled switches keep the same name.

interfaces.name: ACCESSIBILITY_STYLESHEET
interfaces.requirement: The shell entry must import this stylesheet after every component stylesheet. src/main.tsx already does (last of the style imports). The test checks this order.

limitations: The unnamed-Switch finding was not reproduced in static markup. The existing shell-runtime audit already resolved these names through <label for>, and it passed before this change. The change makes the name explicit with aria-labelledby and aria-describedby. It is a robustness fix, not a demonstrated bug fix.

Tests are static: react-dom/server markup and stylesheet text. No DOM, no computed styles, no browser forced-colors or reduced-motion rendering, and no screen reader. Nothing here claims what assistive technology announces.
Click, keyboard toggling and focus behaviour of Switch are unchanged and not exercised by these tests.
Icon-only Button usages are not audited by this milestone. Only Switch naming was in scope.
docs/autopilot-shell-runtime.md, tests/autopilot-shell-runtime.test.mjs and docs/autopilot-result.accessibility.json are not owned by this milestone and were not edited.

The result file uses the path assigned in the task prompt (docs/milestone-result.a11y.json), not the docs/autopilot-result.<role>.json convention from AGENTS.md. The captain should confirm which path it reads.
